newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Five Timorese seek asylum in Spanish mission.
newsitem.headline: Five Timorese seek asylum in Spanish mission.

text.p: Five East Timorese have entered the Spanish Embassy in Jakarta seeking asylum, the official Antara news agency reported on Friday.
Antara quoted an official of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) as confirming the five had entered the embassy compound on Wednesday.
"We have been notified of this but we have not taken any action as they (the Timorese) are still negotiating with the embassy officers," ICRC spokeswoman Sri Wahyu Endah was quoted as telling Antara.
Spanish diplomats, when contacted by Reuters, would not comment on the case and refered all inquiries to the Foreign Ministry in Madrid.
ICRC officials were not available late on Friday.
"If they want to go to Portugal, we will facilitate their departure. But if they want to go to Spain, it would be up to the Spanish government," Endah said.
Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975 and annexed the territory a year later. The United Nations still regards Portugal as the administering authority.
Since September last year, 84 East Timorese have been granted asylum in Portugal after entering foreign embassies in Jakarta. All have had their travel facilitated by the ICRC.
